summary: Environment analysis for the A100 correctness-only run completed. Probed and classified all 20 capabilities the chip input's build/execution path needs, each with its exact command and output in docs/compiler-agent/ENVIRONMENT.md. Ran three end-to-end smokes under the declared QEMU endpoint (-cpu max,vlen=1024,elen=64,vext_spec=v1.0): a C program via the cross gcc, a raw-syscall assembly program via as+ld (guest exit code 42 preserved), and an RVV check (vlenb=128 plus executed vector instructions) with a vlen=256 control that fails as required. Rebuilt and re-ran the QEMU instruction-count plugin (IME int8 executed and compared PASS, smt.vmadot counted; empty-list control on a non-matrix binary; bf16 probe still fails - known gap), the persistent-pool worker probe at 1/2/4/8 guest threads (distinct tids, full coverage, one pool init), the native transport round trip (pack_case -> run-riscv.sh -> native_bundle -> unpack_outputs: alias/relocation and bfloat16 cases compared PASS) and the x86 Triton CPU reference through run-reference.sh (masked vector-add PASS). Recorded 15 facts (14 RUNTIME_PROBE, 1 EMPIRICAL, all origin=input, all with probe-command provenance) and 2 assumptions in PROJECT_STATE.json. Three items classified present+unusable with attempted commands and errors: BF16 IME format selection, MCPM control CSR from userspace, and the SpacemiT LLVM package (host glibc too old; not on the declared build path). No timing, speedup or performance measurement was recorded or required (correctness_only).
